extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, patent attorneys, and parties involved in USPTO disciplinary proceedings (OED staff, counsel)
extracted.subtask_description: Administrative-final-order format describing approval of an Affidavit of Resignation under 37 C.F.R. §11.27 and the resulting exclusion-on-consent from practice before the USPTO, including legal authority, required acknowledgements, publication duties, compliance obligations, and reinstatement presumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to approve affidavit and exclude on consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.27, the USPTO Director has the authority to approve an Affidavit of Resignation and to exclude a practitioner on consent from practice before the Office in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order must be entered by the Director (or on behalf of the Director) and implements exclusion under the cited statutory and regulatory provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of Resignation must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's Affidavit of Resignation must satisfy the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a), including that the consent be freely and voluntarily rendered and the respondent be aware of the investigation and consequences of consenting to exclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The affidavit should expressly state voluntariness (no coercion or duress), awareness of a pending OED investigation (cite of OED file), acknowledgment of alleged facts/investigation scope, and consent to exclusion. The Director determines whether the affidavit complies with § 11.27(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Express awareness and description of OED investigation and allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: The respondent must acknowledge awareness that the OED Director opened an investigation and that the investigation obtained information about specific factual allegations (employment history, formation/control of an outside entity, concealment of conflicts, preparation of invoices, approvals, payments, deposit of funds, and alleged criminal conduct).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The affidavit typically enumerates the factual bases the investigation uncovered (examples here include formation of PSG, concealment from employer HDI, monthly fraudulent invoices from 2000–2014, payments totaling $4,841,146.09, and alleged theft/conversion under state law). Including those factual descriptions in the affidavit supports the Director's decision to accept exclusion on consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of disciplinary rule violations the OED alleges
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director's opinion may identify specific provisions of the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility and/or the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct that the respondent is alleged to have violated (here: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(a), § 10.23(b)(3), § 10.23(b)(4), § 10.23(b)(6), and 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(b), § 11.804(c), § 11.804(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order summarizes the regulatory provisions and the nature of the proscribed conduct: disreputable/gross misconduct; illegal conduct involving moral turpitude; conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation; other conduct adversely reflecting on fitness to practice; and committing criminal acts that reflect adversely on honesty/trustworthiness/fitness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal applicability of Code vs Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility (37 C.F.R. § 10.20 et seq.) applies to practitioner misconduct that occurred prior to May 3, 2013; the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct (37 C.F.R. § 11.101 et seq.) apply to misconduct on or after May 3, 2013.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When alleging violations, the applicable ethical regime depends on the dates of the respondent's conduct; the affidavit and OED opinion should reflect which rules are implicated based on timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of acceptance: exclusion on consent and effective date
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Director determines the Affidavit of Resignation complies with § 11.27(a), the respondent shall be excluded on consent from practice before the Office in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters commencing on the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order must state the effective date of exclusion and formally order approval of the affidavit and exclusion on consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice requirements following exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order in the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's electronic FOIA Reading Room and shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette that is materially consistent with the specified notice language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Official Gazette notice should summarize the acceptance of the affidavit, the nature of the pending investigation, the alleged misconduct and the disciplinary rules implicated, and the reinstatement presumptions; OED Reading Room posting must be made publicly accessible at the designated URL.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 following exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 as ordered in the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the Final Order does not restate § 11.58's text, the respondent is required to perform whatever duties § 11.58 imposes (e.g., notice to clients or other post-discipline obligations) as a condition of the exclusion; the Order expressly commands compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement standard and presumptions under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: The respondent acknowledges that, if and when he applies for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60, the OED Director will conclusively presume, for the purpose of determining the reinstatement application, that the facts set forth in the OED file are true and that the respondent could not have successfully defended against the allegations embodied in the OED Director's opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This acknowledgement is typically included in the affidavit of resignation and limits the respondent's ability to contest the underlying facts for reinstatement purposes; it is a binding concession for the limited purpose of any future reinstatement proceeding under § 11.60.
